issues.legal_issue: For determining the annual value of tenant-occupied property, local taxes are deductible according to the owner's liability under a levy in force, rather than only to the extent actually paid.
material_facts: The assessee owned rented properties and claimed a deduction for municipal taxes levied on them.
The assessee disputed the enhanced extent of its municipal tax liability and had not paid the whole amount claimed.
The municipal levy remained in force during the relevant assessment period.
issues.conclusion: The deductible amount is the local tax the owner is liable to discharge under the levy in force; actual payment is not required, and disputing the levy does not by itself prevent the deduction.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 22 and the proviso to section 23(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, as applicable to the relevant assessment year, annual value is a notional amount, not an amount of actual receipt. The proviso deducts the local taxes for which the owner is responsible, rather than making the deduction depend on when or whether payment is made. A pending challenge to the levy does not defeat the deduction while the levy remains in force. The Court relied on Bhagwan Dass Jain v. Union of India.

rule.if: house_property_income_assessment and tenant_occupied_property and local_tax_levy_in_force and owner_legally_liable_for_local_tax

predicates.house_property_income_assessment: An income assessment determines the annual value of property under the rules for income from house property.
predicates.tenant_occupied_property: A tenant occupies the property being assessed.
predicates.local_tax_levy_in_force: A local authority has imposed a tax on the property and the levy remains in force.
predicates.owner_legally_liable_for_local_tax: The owner is legally responsible for discharging the local tax liability.

issues.definition: When an assessment determines the annual value of tenant-occupied property and a local tax levy in force makes the owner liable for the tax, the owner's tax liability is deductible.
